newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal utilities may launch telecom rival.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal utilities may launch telecom rival.

text.p: Three Portuguese state-owned energy companies said on Thursday that they were considering joining forces to launch a new national telecoms concern.

EDP-Electricidade de Portugal and gas companies Transgas and GDP-Gas de Portugal said in a statement that they had formed a consortium to study the technical and economic aspects of such a venture. They did not say how long the study would take.
The local telecommunications market is dominated, with the exception of the mobile phone business, by the state-controlled Portugal Telecom.

But the Socialist government had been known to favour the entry of the energy companies into the business which will have to be thrown open to competition anyway within a few years under European Union rules.
The energy companies already have networks that could serve as the frameworks for a telecommunications operation.
But analysts said that they saw no immediate threat to Portugal Telecom from the entry of a rival operator.
They said that they doubted that any venture launched by the energy companies could compete with Telecom in the household phone market.

The area in which Telecom would be most vulnerable would be in closed-system operations for large corporate users but this was a market where international companies could already provide alternatives, they said.
"It is not easy to see how these companies would be able to provide individual (phone) services," said analyst Jose Antonio Goncalves of brokers Tottadealer in Lisbon.
"What they could sell would be packages of services to big clients."
Analysts said that investors in Portugal Telecom, 49 percent of whose capital is on the market, had already discounted the fact that rivals would eventually appear on the scene.
Portugal is committed to liberalising fully its telecommunications market by the end of the decade.
"It would probably be good for the government to already have a second operator in place as a deterent to foreign predators," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
